item.title: Wildfire danger in Europe shifts to Greece as evacuation orders remain in France
item.description: For Greece, the danger carried grim resonance: a 2018 wildfire​ at the seaside community of Mati​, near Athens, killed 104 people.

item.title: U.S. probes if Iran was behind cyberattack on utilities in Michigan, Minnesota
item.description: Malicious cyber activity affected technology at water systems in at least seven states this week, including Minnesota, leading authorities to dig into whether Iranian actors are behind the attack, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Savannah Guthrie asks for answers about mom Nancy after notes released
item.description: Savannah Guthrie said she and her family have been "in agony and despair ever since" her mother Nancy's disappearance in February.

item.title: Iran accuses U.S. of escalating tensions as Washington plans more strikes
item.description: Iran accused the U.S. of escalating tensions in the region and said it's preparing its own response if Washington goes ahead with new strikes.

item.title: DOJ to dismiss Reflecting Pool vandalism charges, citing "botched installation"
item.description: Federal prosecutors moved to dismiss an indictment charging U.S. Olympic canoeist David Hearn with ripping the bottom of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, saying the damage was caused by "botched installation and not vandalism."

item.title: 10 climbers, including famed mountaineer, dead in Pakistan avalanche
item.description: The 10-person expedition lost contact with its base camp after an avalanche struck Broad Peak as they attempted to scale the mountain.

item.title: FTC fines ticket reselling company Elite Events and Tickets
item.description: Last year, "CBS Saturday Morning" spoke with ticket reselling company Elite Events and Tickets about its methodology and practices. Now, the Federal Trade Commission is fining the company, saying it violated the Better Online Ticket Sales Act. Elite Events and Tickets neither admitted to nor denied the FTC's allegations.

item.title: Police release Nancy Guthrie ransom notes in hopes of public help
item.description: It has been six months since Nancy Guthrie, the mother of "Today Show" co-host Savannah Guthrie, vanished from her Arizona home. Investigators have now released two ransom notes with "distinctive linguistic characteristics" and are asking for the public's help in identifying their writer.

item.description: Oscar-winning Irish musician Glen Hansard, 56, died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin this week. "CBS Saturday Morning" remembers Hansard, a friend of the show who joined us for multiple Saturday Sessions.

item.description: Japanese alcoholic beverage sake is rising in popularity across the United States. Acclaimed sommelier Daniel Bennett at Chicago's Omakase Room explains more about this beloved rice wine.

item.title: "Video Killed the Radio Star": MTV's impact, 45 years later
item.description: On August 1, 1981 MTV network launched its historic first broadcast. The burgeoning network went from a shoestring budget to one of the most powerful forces in entertainment and music history. Here's a look back on the impact, 45 years later.

item.title: Spain to put containment fence around Ceuta after migrants rush border

item.title: A brief timeline of Iranian cyberattacks on the U.S.
item.description: Investigators are probing whether Iranian hackers are behind this week's malicious cyber activity against water systems in Minnesota. If they are found to be the culprits, it would not be the first time.

item.title: Families sue Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube over deaths of 4 teens
item.description: The families of four children who died by suicide allege that using social media led to depression, anxiety and other mental health problems.

item.title: What records reveal about Newsom's taxpayer-funded, California-branded free diaper program
item.description: CBS California Investigates reviewed 356 pages of state records behind California's $6.2 million diaper contract with Baby2Baby. Here is what they show.

item.title: Newsom's office called our diaper contract reporting "demonstrably false." State records show what happened
item.description: Gov. Newsom's office says the no-bid deal was "competitive," the records weren't delayed, and our reporting is false. The state's own database, deadlines, and the Legislature's budget bills say otherwise. Here's the point-by-point review.

item.title: Newsom's "competitive bid" diaper deal wasn't. California's budget includes dozens of similar no-bid exemptions.
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom said the $6.2 million Baby2Baby contract "went through a competitive bidding process." State records reveal it didn't. CBS California Investigates found dozens of similar no-bid deals in the state budget worth over $1 billion.

item.title: California still hasn't released Baby2Baby diaper contract as lawmakers weigh longer public records delays
item.description: The Newsom administration waited 24 days to decide if it would even let Californians see the multi-million-dollar contract with Baby2Baby, a nonprofit linked to First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom.

item.title: Critics got California's free diaper math wrong, but state won't release key Baby2Baby records
item.description: A CBS News California fact-check found the state's free diaper program won't cost taxpayers 50 cents per diaper, as viral posts claimed. But the Newsom administration still won't release the Baby2Baby contract or competitive bid records amid concerns free diapers could go to waste.

item.title: Dr. Anthony Fauci on pandemics, partisan critics, and "the psyche of the country"
item.description: Millions today owe their lives to the work of the man who devoted his career to public health, but in recent years Dr. Anthony Fauci has been targeted by a partisan, anti-science spectrum of opponents.
